claim: pgvector supports four vector types: vector (4 bytes/dim, up to 16,000 dims), halfvec (2 bytes/dim, up to 16,000 dims), sparsevec (up to 16,000 non-zero elements), and bit (up to 64,000 dims).
quote: vector: Up to 16,000 dimensions, storing 4 bytes per dimension; halfvec: half-precision floats (2 bytes per dimension); sparsevec: Up to 16,000 non-zero elements; bit: Binary vectors up to 64,000 dimensions

claim: The four distance operators are <-> (Euclidean/L2), <#> (negative inner product), <=> (cosine distance), and <+> (taxicab/L1 distance).
quote: `<->` Euclidean (L2) distance | `<#>` Negative inner product | `<=>` Cosine distance | `<+>` Taxicab (L1) distance

claim: Basic usage: CREATE TABLE items (id bigserial PRIMARY KEY, embedding vector(3)); INSERT INTO items (embedding) VALUES ('[1,2,3]'); and nearest-neighbor SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY embedding <-> '[3,1,2]' LIMIT 5.
The pgvector/pgvector GitHub repository has approximately 21,679 stars as of June 2026.

pgvector 0.7.0 added the halfvec and sparsevec types plus L1 distance, hamming_distance and jaccard_distance functions; indexing limits are ~4,000 dims for halfvec and ~1,000 nonzero dims for sparsevec.
quote: pgvector version 0.7.0 added new vector types, including halfvec (2-byte floats; indexing up to 4,000 dimensions) and sparsevec (indexing up to 1,000 nonzero dimensions)

claim: Embeddings are generated client-side by an embedding model (e.g. OpenAI text-embedding-3-small) then written to a vector column; OpenAI embeddings use 1536 dimensions and a cosine-distance query looks like ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector LIMIT 4.
quote: embedding generation happens in the client.embeddings.create() method ... CREATE TABLE documents ( id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, content TEXT, embedding VECTOR(1536) ) ... ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector LIMIT 4. The `<=>` operator calculates cosine distance

claim: Workflow: enable the extension (create extension vector), a model generates the embedding array for text, the array is inserted into a vector(n) column, and similarity search uses ORDER BY embedding <-> query LIMIT k, enabling RAG.
quote: A model creates embeddings ... inserted into a Postgres table with a vector column ... SELECT * FROM items WHERE category_id = 123 ORDER BY embedding <-> '[3,1,2]' LIMIT 5; ... valuable for retrieval augmented generation (RAG)
